key_insight: Brain-Adapter uses a dual-stream MIL design to turn raw 3D brain CT scans and text reports into scan-level multi-label diagnosis without dense annotations.
clinical_relevance: This could make acute intracranial pathology detection more scalable in emergency neuroimaging by reducing manual labeling burden while improving diagnostic robustness.
method: Text-Conditioned Attention uses diagnostic sentences as semantic queries to align image regions with disease concepts.
A parallel visual MIL stream learns global scan-level features from structured labels extracted by an LLM.
An uncertainty-aware refinement module fuses the two streams and resolves ambiguous predictions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing Brain-Adapter outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL baselines on comprehensive 3D CT diagnosis.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of report text, LLM-extracted labels, and careful validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
